pr_comments: Some/many vue and html tests fail because the order of the `childBundles` seems to change, the tests pass on my machine. Is the order important?

Awesome work, really excited about this! 🎉 

Will take a look soon.

Running with HMR also adds the sourcemaps of bundle-url.js and css-loader.js into the CSS sourcemap. But these two are packaged into a seperate JS bundle which should also have it's own sourcemap bundle? (This happens without this PR as well).
Many tests fail because `assertBundleTree`'s order on childbundles is inconsistent (pass on my machine but not on CI)

One last thing and this should be ready:
The `--no-source-maps` flag isn't being cached properly, I think there are two ways to handle this:
- Invalidate the cache based on `--no-source-maps` (so basically re-run the asset)
- Always output sourcemaps in the Asset (performance?) and don't output a SourceMapBundle if the flag is passed

```bash
$ parcel build index.html --no-source-maps

dist/test.7f0ab984.js     1.14 KB    1.40s
dist/index.html             113 B    587ms
dist/test.8d042a79.css       27 B    1.09s

$ parcel build index.html

dist/test.7f0ab984.js     1.14 KB    66ms
dist/index.html             113 B    15ms
dist/test.8d042a79.css       27 B    14ms
```

issue_context.title: linked node_modules source maps are mixed w/ project

<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

# 🐛 bug report

I am trying to include sourcemaps for a dependency that has been linked. `npm link mydep`

This is working with the caveat that the sourcemaps appear under the same root `src/` in chrome devtools. This is a problem b/c the linked node_module sourcemaps appear mixed with my applications sourcemaps and will be overwritten by my app if any conflicts exist.

possibly related to #1801?

<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue here -->

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

<!--- If describing a bug, tell us what your babel configuration looks like -->

```js
{
  "presets": [
    [
      "@babel/preset-env",
      {
        "modules": false,
        "targets": {
          "browsers": [
            "> 1%",
            "last 3 versions",
            "ie >= 9",
            "ios >= 8",
            "android >= 4.2"
          ]
        },
        "useBuiltIns": false
      }
    ]
  ],
  "plugins": [
    ["styled-components", { "displayName": true }],
    "@babel/plugin-proposal-class-properties"
  ]
}
```

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

<!--- Tell us what should happen -->

I would expect any sourcemaps found for node_modules would be served at a different root. See next section for an example

## 😯 Current Behavior

<!--- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->

<!--- If you are seeing an error, please include the full error message and stack trace -->

currently they are served from the same `/src` root.

ex.

app
```
-- src
  -- index.js
```

mydep
```
-- src
  -- index.js
  -- cache
    -- index.js
```

The source maps in chrome devtools will appear as:

```
-- src
  -- index.js (this is from app)
  -- cache
    -- index.js (this is from mydep)
```

I would expect them to appear as:
The source maps in chrome devtools will appear as:

```
-- mydep (or even as a sub dir of node_modules)
  -- index.js
  -- cache
    -- index.js
-- src
  -- index.js
```
## 💁 Possible Solution

<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug -->

## 🔦 Context

<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->

Being able to correctly view sourcemaps for linked dependencies is useful when attempting to debug a package.

## 💻 Code Sample

<!-- Please provide a code repository, gist, code snippet or sample files to reproduce the issue -->

just link any node_module w/ built source maps to your app

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 1.10.1
| Node             | v8.11.3
| npm              | 6.4.1
| Operating System | macos

👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->

review_comments: @devongovett ?
At first, I thought `SourceMapPackager.shouldAddAsset` could be used for this, but it doesn't get called at all.

Yeah I think we will need to add a `map` property to renditions themselves rather than having a the map be a separate rendition since only one rendition of the same type is supported (and there would be no way to associate them). Then, we'll need to special case source maps in the Bundler to create the `map` bundles. Perhaps in `Bundle#addAsset` we could add the map to a sibling `map` bundle? https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/master/packages/core/parcel-bundler/src/Bundle.js#L39
Oh right... hmm

This will be easier in Parcel 2 which supports multiple renditions of the same type. For now, maybe you could move this conversion from array to object into the Bundler after adding assets to the bundles (createBundleTree). We just need to make sure it is converted before running Packagers for backwards compatibility. Additionally, you'll need to associate a source map with the JS/CSS bundle so the correct URL to the source map can be added. This is kind of a hack, but I'm ok with it if it works since Parcel 2 will clean it up.

>  For now, maybe you could move this conversion from array to object into the Bundler after adding assets to the bundles (createBundleTree). We just need to make sure it is converted before running Packagers for backwards compatibility

1. Assets are added by createBundleTree via Bundle#addAsset
2. Transform asset.generated to generatedMap
3. Run packagers: JSAsset calls Bundle#addAsset for bundle loaders 🙈 

Even worse:
https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/6cbf2a65cdcd66af135ff9eca2a3799bde9f8a5b/packages/core/parcel-bundler/src/packagers/JSPackager.js#L214-L216
First returns the untransformed generated format and then the transformed one.
I've chosen a different approach ~(loading sourcemaps from previous asset stages doesn't work yet)~
@devongovett ?

> How can/why should a bundle be a child bundle and a sibling bundle at the same time?

Yeah, it's weird. The bundle tree data structure was added to over time, but needed to retain backward compatibility. It'll be MUCH nicer in Parcel 2.

It is possible that the current data structure is insufficient for what we need to do in Parcel 1. Either we could wait for Parcel 2, or make some modifications/hacks to Parcel 1 to make it work. I am not against adding hacks, but I'm also fine with waiting for this feature until Parcel 2 and perhaps starting on the implementation there instead. What do you think?

In the PostCSS docs it says `to` is required for generating valid sourcemaps, not sure why it has been removed.

Although it probably doesn't matter as parcel's sourcemap bundler overwrites this anyways.

The postcss docs say for `parse`:
![bildschirmfoto 2019-01-05 um 18 10 40](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4586894/50727021-428c7f00-1115-11e9-9d72-88169208d60e.png)
So `to` was never used in that call
